newsitem.title: USA: Fed shouldn't up rates - ex-Labor Secretary Reich.
newsitem.headline: Fed shouldn't up rates - ex-Labor Secretary Reich.

text.p: The Federal Reserve should not raise interest rates on Tuesday, former Labor Secretary Robert Reich said on Monday.
"I do not believe the Fed should be raising rates tomorrow," Reich told a luncheon meeting sponsored by the Center for National Policy. "We don't see any sign of accelerating inflation."
Reich, who left the administration last year, is now a professor at Brandeis University's Heller Graduate School.

Jerry Jasinowski, President of the National Association of Manufacturers, agreed that there was no need for the U.S. central bank to raise interest rates, noting that economic growth is slowing anyway.

Jasinowski also argued that the economy can generally grow more quickly than most economist believe because of structural changes. "There are still limits, but those limits are closer to three percent (annual) growth," he said.
Both Jasinowski and Reich though did say that they believed that the Fed has done a good job in sustaining the economic expansion.
